removed_lines: pope john paul award ceremony, carlow the pope john paul award is a national award which acknowledges young people for their involvement in parish and community life.
the award was set up in memory of pope john paul and is rooted in his belief in the goodness of young people.
in our diocese hundreds of teenagers receive the award at bronze, silver or gold level each year from bishop denis.
the award is open to those in senior cycle in school and above.

it asks the participants to make a commitment to serve their parish and community during the year, along with other young people, and with adult leaders from the school and parish to encourage and support them.
the pope john paul award aims to develop leadership and personal skills in the young people, and to help them to find an active role in their faith journey.

this year, six young people from naas, sallins and two mile house received their awards at the end of september, and we thank each of them for the contribution which they have made to the parish, the schools and to the wider community.
congratulations to each one on their achievement!

registration for the award is now open for this year, and we are happy to invite those young people from ty and above who are interested to contact trish in the parish office for information on how to register.
